verdict.tagline: Rewind time and face heavy choices in a gripping episodic drama

you want to explore alternate choices without restarting
not_for_you_if: you dislike unskippable dialogue and cutscenes
you prefer stories without heavy cliffhangers

The game starts with the main character trying to hide from a tornado inside a lighthouse, only to wake up and realize it was just a dream. That is how the game welcomes you, the critically acclaimed Alan Wa...it a second. Wrong game. That is actually how you are introduced to the critically acclaimed Life is Strange, though you would be forgiven for the initial mix-up.

Step into the shoes of Max Caulfield as she navigates Arcadia Bay, a small town in the middle of nowhere facing some seriously paranormal stuff. If that specific setup feels instantly familiar, it is because the atmosphere borrows heavily from Stephen King, a man who has made an entire career out of trapping ordinary people in bizarre, isolated situations. The structural similarities to Alan Wake don't stop at the lighthouse intro, either. The game fully embraces a television-like episodic format, which is also highly reminiscent of the classic Telltale Games formula. This structure gives the narrative a deliberate, cliffhanger-heavy pacing that makes it incredibly hard to put down once you start.

But Arcadia Bay holds much deeper, darker secrets than just impending strange weather. You are immediately thrust into a dense narrative web involving the mysterious disappearance of a local girl, Rachel Amber, and the looming threat of an apocalyptic tornado. As you pull on these threads, you quickly cross paths with Nathan Prescott, a volatile, wealthy classmate whose erratic behavior and dangerous connections tie into the town's darker underbelly, adding a layer of grounded human malice to the supernatural dread. To deal with it all, Max unlocks unexpected time-bending superpowers. Funny enough, these time shenanigans mark yet another similarity to a Remedy project, only this time the timeline is flipped. Life is Strange actually beat Quantum Break to the punch.

At its core, the game is incredibly charming, even if it wears its heart on its sleeve. It honestly feels like playing through 13 Reasons Why…

I always loved the idea of choices matter games the fact that literally like 90% of games arnt choice games wanted more after finishing walking dead and i saw one name pop up life is strange i got it for like 3 euro on humble bundle since i played the demo on my xbox a lot i got the full game w no spoilers every time i would load up an episode i would be blown away by the twists and how your choices bites you in the ass  Also the vibe was really nice it was like very mysterious yet being cool 

to be honest i liked this game i loved episode 5 the most i thought the game pulled a ddlc on me in the dream part. i really liked davids redemption and the insane plot twist in episode 3 & 4 i would've loved a no rewind but then again it doesnt make it bad, i wasnt attached to the characters but i loved  max a lot i found her relatable again the story is great but not gut wrenching for me  there are many people who got their life changed by this game i still think that you should'nt spoil yourself i really enjoyed it i'll replay again in my life

cohorts.summary: The time-rewinding mechanic allows players to test alternate outcomes and face heavy narrative dilemmas, beginning with a free introductory episode.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features a mechanic allowing players to rewind time.

citations.review_text:
This game has a neat mystery and a fun gameplay gimmick. Being able to rewind time is a fantastic mechanic for a Choose Your Adv style game, it fits this game SO well!
The story is melodramatic as hell, and I think that works to the games advantage. Somehow this game is such a powerful time capsule despite not being THAT old. It has an atmosphere to the game that can really sink into your bones. Several areas in the game I just sat back and chilled to the music.

I think you'll either love or hate this game. Past all the story beast, characters, and dubious depictions, the game just has a "vibe" to it that is hard to explain but easy to see. If you try the first episode and like it a lot, I promise you the rest of the episodes will be enjoyable too.

This story must go hard if you're 14. I just don't see the hype about this game or why people adore it so much. Story starts like your average highschool drama and then at the end [spoiler] you have to save arcadia bay from the hurricane i somehow caused by traveling in the past too much (?) [/spoiler] characters do not get enough time or enough writing to make you actually feel anything for them and with max's new time travelling powers you can go back in time to undo/change a choice you made (except for 2) which kills the sense of responsibility but just cool enough to make you see other outcomes without having to do another playthrough. The time travelling gimmick could have been much more but it always felt like it never really used its full potential. [spoiler] none of the choices you make through the game matter at the very end since you get to choose between sacrificing your friend (everyone lives except for chloe) or sacrifice all of arcadia bay (everyone dies except for chloe and max) what the ♥♥♥♥? [/spoiler] there must have been some hypnosis or brain wash in the game that won "awards" and made grown ass people cry their eyes out and for this game to have 173k positive reviews, so much so that people fall into depression after completing it? These people would kill themselves if they played the first season of the walking dead. What a lame mosh-pit "shakabrah"

Life is Strange is a story based game released in January 30th 2015. For a game released in early 2015 it still holds up today. and with the release of the remastered version in February of 2022 (And its 'Before The Storm' prequel) its a game you can always, no matter the time. Or scenario you can always return to the game, and play a episode or even just walk around and admire the visuals, that this game Shows.
 
The graphic almost Picturesque art style, is truly captivating. And the story, oh boy the story. Going from discovering you can reverse time, to instances of kidnapping and murders, and the looming threat of the tornado reminding you that max's time is winding down, can be truly overwhelming, which helps amerce you into the world, and story of Life Is Strange.

And the plethora of Likeable and Even Dislikeable characters, Allows you to cling, and gravitate your love or appreciation to a certain character, or characters. And in my opinion a game that's easy to form bonds with a certain character, are among some of my favourite's out there.

The Music of Life Is Strange, is one of, if not my all time favourite pieces of music from a game. From Syd Matters 'To All Of You' and 'Obstacles' To Local Natives 'Mt Washington' 'Piano Fire' by Sparklehorse And 'Spanish Sahara' By Foals. Are tracks that if you have, or haven't played this game, You should 100% have a listen to this games soundtrack, You wont regret it.

All around, Life Is Strange is a Rollercoaster and a half. And no matter the person you are, you are guaranteed to shed a tear, or feel some kinds of Emotion towards the Ending of this Game, from the journey you go through on this 14 - 15 hour Experience is Quite something. If you are only able to play the first episode, it is still more than enough to get a good enough idea, of the kind of game this is, And if not I urge you to at least, watch a playthrough on Youtube. You Really, Really will not regret it.

Thank You For Reading. x

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game includes an option where the first episode is free to try.

citations.review_text: Fantastic game, I would recommend it to anyone! Without giving any spoilers, the story is 100% worth the time and I will be coming back to this game to replay it. I am excited to play it over again to find things that I may have missed in the first playthrough. I do have to say though, the ending felt a little short and I wish there was more of a satisfying ending to the story. I love the idea of the first episode being free so you can get a feel for the game and decide then if you'd like to purchase it. I cannot recommend enough to try out the first episode and see how you like it! If you do, please don't rush through the game trying to complete it. Take your time and look at everything around you and really soak it all up.

[h3]10000000000/10 best story game ever[/h3]
I fhckinggg love this game... Everything about this game is just so perfect. The characters, the writing, EVERYTHING. The problems and the complexity of the characters are so real, and that's one of the reasons why I love this game so muchhh (ㅠ﹏ㅠ). I really, really love the story of this game. And I actually also love one of the themes of this game, which is the butterfly effect and how even the smallest choices can end up having huge consequences. If you can help other people, you should, even if it's not your responsibility.

YUPPPP, I love the characters. Yeah, even Victoria. She's so cute when she's not being mean and terrorizing everyone. I also feel for Nathan and can sympathize with him because he's obviously just another fxjucked-up teenager with bad past (something definitely happened to him 🙁), but I still hate him at the same time because it doesn't justify what he did. And I also like how Rachel haunts the narrative. (AND SHE'S INSPIRED BY LAURA PALMER???).

The last choice in this game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HARD :( It's either you [spoiler]sacrifice Chloe (going back in time and accepting Chloe's fate, preventing the storm from happening and saving more people) or sacrifice Arcadia Bay (saving Chloe and making sure that she thinks the world doesn't hate her and that she's not alone or abandoned anymore).[/spoiler] .·°՞(っ◜ᯅ◝ς)՞°·.

lawbbb this game. I still feel so empty after finishing it and making that last decision :( And I got all the achievements mwehehe :3

This game is not just a game... it's an experience I'll never forget. Every episode had me smiling, stressing, crying, and just sitting there staring at the screen after the credits rolled. Max and Chloe will always have a special place in my heart. The soundtrack, the vibes, the small moments... everything hits so hard. I wish I could erase my memory just to experience it for the first time again. It's crazy how a game from years ago still feels this emotional. 1000% recommended if you love story-driven games. Absolute masterpiece, and the nostalgia after finishing it is unreal.
